name: Brine metal binder
subtitle: a designed protein that picks lithium from brine

effect: a learned model predicts a protein's 3D shape from its sequence
how: Lithium is pulled from brine by leaving it in evaporation ponds for a year and a half, which wastes water and only works in a few deserts. Proteins grip metal ions by holding oxygen atoms at exact distances, and shape-prediction tools now let that cage be designed for one ion and against its near twins. A column of such proteins on a fibre support could take lithium from seawater or oilfield brine in an afternoon and release it with a change of acidity.
obstacle: The protein must survive thousands of grip-and-release cycles in hot salt before it beats a pond that costs nothing to run.
why: Metal-binding design is advancing fast; durability in industrial brine is the open question.
real: Designed lithium-binding proteins are an active funded program (an ARIA-backed UK effort, GBP 6.2M, screening thousands of protein variants for Li/Na-selective membranes; a 2026 grant to deep-learn Li-binding scaffolds and yeast-display screen them) but no peer-reviewed designed-protein sorbent run on brine in a column was found.
